title_en: Letter to Victor of Rome on the Date of Pascha
author: Polycrates of Ephesus
addressee: Victor, bishop of Rome, and the Roman church
occasion: Victor of Rome had demanded that the churches of Asia Minor abandon their Quartodeciman practice of observing Pascha on the fourteenth of the month and conform to the Roman custom. Polycrates writes on behalf of the Asian bishops to defend their tradition.
argument: Polycrates insists that the Asian churches observe the day of Pascha without adding or subtracting anything, following the gospel and the rule of faith. He appeals to the great figures buried in Asia—Philip, John, Polycarp, Thraseas, Sagaris, Papirius, and Melito—who all kept the fourteenth day. He adds his own authority as the eighth bishop in his family and as one who has studied all holy scripture and consulted brethren throughout the world. He declares that he is not frightened by threats, since one must obey God rather than men. He notes that the bishops he could mention, whom Victor had asked him to summon, approved his letter.

outline.move: Polycrates defends the Asian Quartodeciman observance of Pascha by citing the great saints buried in Asia who kept it, his own family tradition, and the principle that one must obey God rather than men.

cast.name: Polycrates
cast.who: Bishop of Ephesus, the author, who writes as the eighth bishop in his family line.

cast.name: Victor
cast.who: Bishop of Rome, the implied addressee who demanded the Asian churches change their Paschal observance.

cast.name: Philip
cast.who: One of the twelve apostles, said to be buried at Hierapolis with two aged virgin daughters.

cast.name: John
cast.who: The disciple who reclined on the Lord's breast; described as a priest who wore the petalon, a martyr and teacher, buried at Ephesus.

cast.name: Polycarp
cast.who: Bishop and martyr buried at Smyrna.

cast.name: Thraseas
cast.who: Bishop and martyr from Eumeneia, buried at Smyrna.

cast.name: Sagaris
cast.who: Bishop and martyr buried at Laodicea.

cast.name: Papirius
cast.who: Called 'the blessed,' mentioned among the Asian figures.

cast.name: Melito
cast.who: Called 'the eunuch,' who conducted himself in all things in the Holy Spirit and lies at Sardis awaiting the visitation from heaven.

voices.speaker: Polycrates (author)
voices.how_marked: First-person singular throughout; the letter is his own voice.

key_terms.sense: Without tampering or falsification; keeping the day exactly as received.
Great foundational figures or luminaries of the Asian churches now buried there.
The coming of the Lord in glory from heaven to raise the saints.
The high priest's golden plate or diadem, indicating John's priestly dignity.
The fourteenth day of the month on which the Asian churches observed Pascha.
The rule or standard of faith which the Asian churches followed without deviation.
Leaven; the people removed leaven at the time the Asian churches kept the day.

key_terms.source_term: πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ Θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις
key_terms.sense: The principle that obedience to God takes precedence over obedience to human authority.
Grey hair; Polycrates says he has not borne grey hair in vain but has lived in Christ Jesus.

scripture: The fragment contains no direct scriptural citations. The phrase 'πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ Θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις' echoes Acts 5:29. The reference to 'the day of the coming of the Lord' reflects New Testament language about the parousia. No LXX or Vulgate book names or Psalm numbering appear in the fragment.
uncertain: The exact date of the letter within the late second century; it is usually placed around 190–195 CE during Victor's episcopate, but the fragment itself gives no date.
The identity of Papirius beyond the epithet 'the blessed.'
Whether the 'greater ones' are the luminaries just listed or other unnamed authorities.
The precise nature of the 'threats' (καταπλησσομένοις) Polycrates refers to; the fragment does not specify them.
Whether the bishops Polycrates mentions were actually summoned and present, or whether he is speaking rhetorically about those he could mention.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Papirius: Called 'the blessed,' mentioned among the Asian figures.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Papirius: Called 'the blessed' (μακάριον), but the brief should note that unlike the others, he is not given the titles 'bishop and martyr' or described with any ecclesiastical office in the source.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Melito: Called 'the eunuch,' who conducted himself in all things in the Holy Spirit and lies at Sardis awaiting the visitation from heaven.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Μελίτωνα τὸν εὐνοῦχον, τὸν ἐν ἁγίῳ πνεύματι πάντα πολιτευσάμενον· ὃς κεῖται ἐν Σάρδεσι περιμένων τὴν ἀπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν ἐπισκοπὴν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Melito: Called 'the eunuch' (τὸν εὐνοῦχον), who conducted himself in all things in the Holy Spirit (τὸν ἐν ἁγίῳ πνεύματι πάντα πολιτευσάμενον), who lies at Sardis awaiting the visitation from heaven (τὴν ἀπὸ τῶν οὐρανῶν ἐπισκοπὴν). The brief should note that like Papirius, he is not called 'bishop and martyr' in the source.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He appeals to the great figures buried in Asia—Philip, John, Polycarp, Thraseas, Sagaris, Papirius, and Melito—who all kept the fourteenth day.
_unresolved_facts.fix: He appeals to the great figures buried in Asia—Philip with his three daughters, John, Polycarp, Thraseas, Sagaris, Papirius, and Melito—who all kept the fourteenth day. (The source mentions three daughters of Philip: two aged virgins buried at Hierapolis and a third who lived in the Holy Spirit and rests at Ephesus.)

_unresolved_facts.claim: He notes that the bishops he could mention, whom Victor had asked him to summon, approved his letter.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐδυνάμην δὲ τῶν ἐπισκόπων τῶν συμπαρόντων μνημονεῦσαι, οὓς ὑμεῖς ἠξιώσατε μετακληθῆναι ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ, καὶ μετεκαλεσάμην· ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐὰν γράφω, πολλὰ πλήθη εἰσίν. οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν μικρόν μου ἄνθρωπον, συνηυδόκησαν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ
_unresolved_facts.fix: He notes that the bishops who were present with him, whom Victor had asked him to summon and whom he did summon, approved his letter. The source says he could mention (μνημονεῦσαι) the bishops who were present (συμπαρόντων), not that he merely 'could mention' them as potential supporters; they were actually present and approved.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He adds his own authority as the eighth bishop in his family and as one who has studied all holy scripture and consulted brethren throughout the world.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἑπτὰ μὲν ἦσαν συγγενεῖς μου ἐπίσκοποι, ἐγὼ δὲ ὄγδοος· καὶ πάντοτε τὴν ἡμέραν ἤγαγον οἱ συγγενεῖς μου, ὅταν ὁ λαὸς ἤρνυε τὴν ζύμην. ἐγὼ οὖν, ἀδελφοὶ, ἑξήκοντα πέντε ἔτη ἔχων ἐν Κυρίῳ· καὶ συμβεβληκὼς τοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκουμένης ἀδελφοῖς· καὶ πᾶσαν ἁγίαν γραφὴν διεληλυθὼς
_unresolved_facts.fix: He adds his own authority as the eighth bishop in his family line, noting that his relatives always observed the day when the people removed the leaven. He mentions his sixty-five years in the Lord, his consultation with brethren from throughout the world, and that he has gone through all holy scripture.
